title: Preposition (in/for/about etc.) + -ing
subtitle: interested in doing / without stopping / look forward to doing
summary: After a preposition (in, for, about, before, by, without, to ...) a verb takes the -ing form, including after look forward to and prefer ... to.

lesson.heading: Preposition + -ing
lesson.text: If a preposition (in/for/about etc.) is followed by a verb, the verb ends in **-ing**. You can also say 'instead of somebody doing something', 'fed up with people doing something' etc.

examples.text: Are you interested **in working** for us?
I'm not good **at learning** languages.
Kate must be fed up **with studying**.
What are the advantages **of having** a car?
Thanks very much **for inviting** me to your party.
How **about meeting** for lunch tomorrow?
Why don't you go out **instead of sitting** at home all the time?
Amy went to work **in spite of feeling** ill.
I'm fed up with **people telling** me what to do.

lesson.heading: before -ing / after -ing
lesson.text: We say **before -ing** and **after -ing**. You can also say 'Before I went out ...' and '... after you left school'.

examples.text: **Before going** out, I phoned Sarah.
What did you do **after leaving** school?

lesson.heading: by -ing
lesson.text: We use **by -ing** to say how something happens.

examples.text: You can improve your English **by reading** more.
She made herself ill **by not eating** properly.
Many accidents are caused **by people driving** too fast.
The burglars got into the house **by breaking** a window and **climbing** in.
We ran ten kilometres **without stopping**.
It was a stupid thing to say. I said it **without thinking**.
She needs to work **without people disturbing** her.
I have enough problems of my own **without having** to worry about yours.

lesson.heading: to + -ing (look forward to doing)
lesson.text: We often use **to + infinitive** (*We decided to travel by train.*). But **to** is also a preposition, like in/for/about (*We went from Paris to Geneva. I prefer tea to coffee. Are you looking forward to the weekend?*). When **to** is a preposition and it is followed by a verb, we use **to -ing**.

examples.text: I prefer driving **to travelling** by train.
Are you looking forward **to going** on holiday?
I'm fed up **with travelling** by train. / How **about going** away this weekend?

lesson.text: look forward to, prefer ... to, be used to - here to is a preposition, so the next verb ends in -ing: looking forward to seeing you.

exercises.explanation: After the preposition before, the verb ends in -ing: before going out.

exercises.prompt: Helen has a good memory for names. Helen is good at ___.
exercises.explanation: good at + -ing: good at remembering names.

exercises.prompt: Did you get into trouble because you were late? Did you get into trouble for ___?
We didn't eat at home. We went to a restaurant instead. We went to a restaurant instead of ___.
exercises.explanation: instead of + -ing: instead of eating at home.

exercises.prompt: Match the sentence beginnings with their endings.

pairs.left: The burglars got into the house
It was a stupid thing to say. I said it

exercises.prompt: I was able to reach the top shelf ___ on a chair.
exercises.explanation: by -ing says how something happened: by standing on a chair.

exercises.prompt: Kevin got himself into financial trouble ___ too much money.
exercises.explanation: by -ing: by borrowing too much money.

exercises.prompt: Dan left the hotel without ___ his bill.
Can you touch your toes without ___ your knees?

exercises.explanation: prefer something to something else - here to is a preposition, so the verb is -ing: to travelling.

exercises.prompt: You're going to the dentist tomorrow and you don't enjoy visits to the dentist. Say how you feel.
exercises.answer: I'm not looking forward to going to the dentist.
exercises.explanation: look forward to + -ing: looking forward to going.

exercises.statement: Are you looking forward to go on holiday?
exercises.explanation: Are you looking forward to going on holiday? After look forward to, the verb ends in -ing.
